In the wilds of Sol'Kesh, whether it is the darkened tunnels of the Umbrawells or the wide open vistas of the Farplains, the creatures 
that roam are often coming across a Traveler for the first time in their ancestral memory. With instincts unable to process such an 
novel encounter, Travelers are regularly met with curiosity as much as they are met with hostility. While the temperament and natural 
behavior of many creatures differ wildly, like the keenly observant calitross, to the near mindless rot eater tormull, most creatures are 
capable of a form of familiarity and training. Though the means to do so must be tailored to the type of beast./.
Taming Example

though fierce, this creature is open to both Bond and Control 
methods. As the grahknash is a CR 6 creature with an intelligence 
of 2, this gives it a total Taming Value of 8. Once all segments 
are complete the creature will then be the ally of the traveler 
permanently.

Taming Guidelines
There are certain prerequisites and rules to successfully Tame the 
wild creatures of Sol'Kesh. As well as bonuses to fill the segments.
 
• A Traveler must know as much as they can before entirely 
trusting the animal, and so must Fully Complete a Journal Entry 
on the creature type before attempting to tame one of its kind.
• Not all creatures are tamed the same way, each creature will 
state whether they are open to Bond or Control in their statblock. 
For example, a grahknash is stated as Control 8, meaning it has a 
Taming Gauge of 8 segments. 
• A creature's Taming Gauge segment length is determined 
by their Bond/Control amount (to a minimum of 1) + their 
Intelligence stat number.
• Taming a creature is an intense activity and attempting to 
complete each segment takes a full active day to perform. 
• A creature can be tamed by two methods, determined by their 
Taming Stat on their statblock. To complete a Bond Segment a 
Traveler must succeed in an Animal Handling Check, while a 
Control Segment requires a successful Intimidation Check. It is 
important to tame a creature in a similar fashion. For example, if 
a creature has any completed segments in Bond, and the traveler 
performs a Control action, this contradictory taming method will 
erase any existing progress in the Bond segments.
• When a creature is successful Tamed, it can then be used as a 
mount, a reliable ally, and understands basic spoken commands. 
There is no limit to how many creatures a Traveler can tame. 
• It is important to note that Control is not a form of abuse or 
punishment towards the creatures, but instead means that 
the Traveler is asserting themselves as a leader from a place of 
personal strength and force of will.

What better way for a Traveler to learn about the life around them, then to take an active part in raising the creatures that make up its 
diverse ecosystem. While many beasts are live-born, or discovered as a juvenile and raised through either Bounding or Control. Those 
that lay eggs, such as arthropods, amphibians, avians, lizards, fish, and more, can allow a Traveler with the means to hatch them, a life 
long companion, and in some instances create a true familial bond.
Hunting For Eggs
Unlike Scavenging, searching for a creature's unborn young does 
not require the death of the creature. Simply being in an area that 
is known to host the animal and their kin, is enough for a Traveler 
to attempt an Intelligence (Nature) check, the DC being entirely 
unique to each creature and found on their Statblock. 
Once an egg is found, being plucked from its natural environment 
can result in a premature death for the young if not taken care 
of quickly. Waterborne eggs from the Strands or Fenlands must 
be kept within a container of salt or fresh water immediately, 
lest they expire within 10 minutes of exposure. Furthermore, any 
discovered eggs must be placed in a biome specific incubator or it 
will spoil and kill the young within.
Failing to find an egg does not result in any risks. Although a 
Keeper may want to consider introducing an encounter from its 
protective parents, whether or not an egg is found if the story 
warrants it.
Hatching and Caring
The work is far from done once the creature emerges from its egg. 
The time it takes for young to hatch and reach maturity varies 
from species to species, and is found listed on their Statblock as 
Seasons (4 seasons per year). When the creature reaches maturity 
it will already be considered Tamed. In addition, such hands-
on experience allows a Traveler to fully complete that creature's 
Journal Entry.
This time spent nuturing the creature can be considered a 
downtime activity, or simply having the creature along with 
them, if a safe and secure method of transport is possible. This is 
quite unique per creature and so it is up to the Keeper's discretion 
on what is possible.
Crafting Incubators
From the minuscule daellash roe to the heavy rock-hard argustaur 
egg, each animal has particular methods to hatch and raise their 
young. While imperfect to capture each need, an incubator that is 
tailored to the biome in which the creature was found is a reliable 
enough method to hatch an egg safely. Incubators are often 
roughly 3 ft. long, 1 ft. wide and 1 ft. high. They may only 
incubate one egg at a time, and can be used indefinitely
once crafted.
